name: Chichewa (Nyanja)
notes: Chichewa/Nyanja (Chicheŵa). Bantu language of Malawi, Zambia, Mozambique and Zimbabwe. The orthography is phonemic and maps closely onto the IPA (Downing & Mtenje 2017 §2.1). KEY FEATURES: (1) FIVE-VOWEL SYSTEM: Downing & Mtenje's chart (4) pairs orthographic e/o with IPA /ɛ ɔ/, which is what this spec emits. (2) IMPLOSIVE VOICED STOPS: their consonant chart (2) gives IPA /ɓ ɗ/ for orthographic <b d>; the pulmonic plosives are kept as second candidates for loans. (3) ASPIRATED SERIES: <ph th kh ch/tch> = [pʰ tʰ kʰ tʃ/tʃʰ]; the <h> spells aspiration of the preceding stop and is never a segment of its own, so the prenasalised aspirates <mph nth nkh ntch> are declared as whole graphemes rather than left to fall apart into a stop plus a stray /h/. (4) PRENASALISED CONSONANTS: <mb mp nd nk nt nz ng> are single onsets; <ng'> is [ŋ] against <ng> [ŋɡ] (Downing & Mtenje chart (3)). (5) LABIALISATION is a general secondary articulation, so the <Cw> series covers the prenasalised and aspirated members too (<ngw ndw mbw mpw nkhw>) and not only the plain stops. (6) <sh> = [ʃ], mainly in loans (Downing & Mtenje chart (2), citing Mchombo 2004 and Watkins 1937). (7) SINGLE LIQUID: the inventory has one liquid, /l/; <r> is the orthographic variant used after front vowels and carries the same phoneme. (8) <ŵ> = [β], retained in the inventory on the Chichewa Board's recommendation despite its marginal status. (9) <h> occurs in only a handful of borrowed words. NOT MODELLED, deliberately: Chichewa contrasts high and low tone lexically, but 'tone is not indicated in Chichewa orthography' (Downing & Mtenje 2017 §2.1), so no grapheme rule can recover it. Nor is there lexical stress — stress is phrasal, realised as penult lengthening over a prosodic phrase, which a word-level spec cannot place. The syllabic nasal is likewise left undeclared: whether preconsonantal <m n> is a syllabic class prefix (m̩-tengo) or the nasal of a prenasalised onset is a morphological fact, invisible to a grapheme rule, and declaring it positionally turned correct prenasalisation into spurious syllabicity.

wikipron.citation: As-scored PER (n=1564, broad+strip_stress convention) is 0.3119. Downing & Mtenje 2017 (The Phonology of Chichewa, OUP) §2.1 state that Chichewa contrasts lexical high and low tone but that 'tone is not indicated in Chichewa orthography'; the spec's notes already record this as deliberately unmodelled. Measured in the wikipron/nya_latn_broad gold: 731/1624 entries (45.0%) carry a combining acute-accent tone mark on a vowel or syllabic nasal, against 0/1624 orthographic headwords marking it (the two NFD hits on plain ŵ/Ŵ are the orthographic letter itself, not a tone diacritic, and were excluded). 59 of the 1564 unique headwords recur in the gold with more than one tone pattern for the identical spelling, direct evidence the orthography underdetermines tone. Folding the acute tone mark out of both hypothesis and gold (grave/circumflex/caron were checked and do not occur in this gold) takes PER to 0.2604. No vowel-length mark (ː or ˑ) occurs anywhere in this gold's 1624 entries, so a length fold was tried and made no difference — a negative result: this gold's broad transcription convention does not record the penultimate lengthening Downing & Mtenje describe, so there is nothing for a length rule to be measured against here. Measured this session against the wikipron/nya_latn_broad.tsv gold; not itself sourced as a target number.
